title: BCG, RD1, and what vaccination is
dek: BCG is a live M. bovis derivative that lost ESX-1 (RD1) and a pile of other RDs depending on the strain. It prevents childhood meningitis and miliary disease better than adult pulmonary cavities.
story: Bacillus Calmette–Guérin is M. bovis passaged until it lost RD1 (ESX-1) and, depending on daughter strains (Pasteur, Danish, Tokyo, Russia, Moreau…), additional RDs. It is still MTBC: NAATs light up, pncA is intrinsically PZA-R, and WGS will call bovis/BCG if you let it.

Efficacy is age- and disease-form-specific. BCG consistently reduces childhood TB meningitis and miliary disease. Protection against adult cavitary pulmonary TB is variable by latitude, prior NTM sensitisation, and strain. It is not a sterilizing vaccine and it is not TPT.

BCG is contraindicated in true MSMD and in untreated advanced HIV in many programmes (policy details vary with ART and CD4). Disseminated BCG-osis is an immunodeficiency until proven otherwise. Bladder BCG for urothelial carcinoma is a separate iatrogenic MTBC exposure.
deepTitle: Strain genetics a lab will actually see
deep: RD1 deletion is shared; RD2 is deleted in some strains (Danish) and not others (Tokyo). Do not use a single RD PCR as a full strain ID.
BCG is IGRA-silent for ESAT-6/CFP-10 (RD1) but TST-positive. That is the point of IGRAs in BCG-vaccinated people.
New TB vaccines (M72/AS01E and others) are a different object — subunit, not live RD1-deleted bovis. Do not file them under BCG.
A “TB” genome from a bladder-cancer ward is BCG until the tree says otherwise.

visual.caption: BCG sits inside MTBC as an RD1-deleted M. bovis derivative. Daughter strains differ by extra RD losses. Clinical Mtb keeps ESX-1.

example.title: Infant with BCG-osis
example.setup: HIV-negative infant, ulcerated BCG site, axillary adenitis, AFB from node, Xpert MTB detected RIF not detected. WGS pending.

steps.title: This may still be BCG
steps.body: Xpert cannot distinguish. Site and age are the clue. WGS/RD1 PCR next.

steps.title: Think host
steps.body: Disseminated BCG is MSMD (IFNGR, IL12RB1, NEMO…) until immunology says no.

steps.title: Do not start BPaLM empirically
steps.body: This is not RR-TB. Management is BCG-osis plus immunology referral; PZA is not active anyway.

example.takeaway: BCG is MTBC with a deletion history and a host-susceptibility context.

check.why: That is also why IGRAs can ignore BCG.

check.prompt: BCG is M. bovis-derived. Expected PZA interpretation is:
choices: Always PZA-S because BCG is a vaccine
Intrinsic PZA-R via the bovis pncA allele — not acquired MDR
PZA-R only if rpoB is mutant
PZA cannot be sequenced because BCG lacks pncA
check.answer: Intrinsic PZA-R via the bovis pncA allele — not acquired MDR
check.why: Do not file BCG pncA under treatment-emergent resistance.

whyWrong.PZA cannot be sequenced because BCG lack: It has pncA; the allele is inactive.

check.prompt: On the BCG hierarchy, why is “not cavities” in the bottom row?
choices: Because BCG sterilizes adult cavities with 100% efficacy
Because BCG’s reliable benefit is against childhood disseminated/meningeal TB, not reliably against adult cavitary pulmonary disease
Because Xpert cannot detect pulmonary TB after BCG
check.answer: Because BCG’s reliable benefit is against childhood disseminated/meningeal TB, not reliably against adult cavitary pulmonary disease
